title: “Loruhamah”, “Loammi”, “Ammi”, “Ruhamah”, “Ishi” — the names the KJV leaves untranslated, and the words the Greek prints
summary: In Hosea 1:6, 1:9, 2:1 and 2:16 the KJV prints the names Loruhamah, Loammi, Ammi, Ruhamah and Ishi. The Hebrew quoted prints each name as ordinary words that appear elsewhere in the same verses, and Brenton’s Greek prints Greek words, which Brenton’s own English gives as “Unpitied”, “Not my people”, “My people”, “Pitied” and “My husband”, where the KJV prints a name.

KJV Hosea 1:9: “Call his name Loammi: for ye are not my people”. Hebrew (WLC) 1:9: לֹ֣א עַמִּ֑י … אַתֶּם֙ לֹ֣א עַמִּ֔י. Brenton’s Greek 1:9: οὐ λαός μου· διότι ὑμεῖς οὐ λαός μου. Brenton’s own English (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/HOS01.htm) prints: “Not my people: for ye are not my people”. KJV Hosea 2:1: “Say ye unto your brethren, Ammi; and to your sisters, Ruhamah”. Hebrew (WLC) 2:3: עַמִּ֑י … רֻחָֽמָה. Brenton’s Greek 2:3: λαός μου, καὶ τῇ ἀδελφῇ ὑμῶν, ἠλεημένη. Brenton’s own English (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/HOS02.htm) prints: “My people, and to your sister, Pitied”. KJV Hosea 2:16: “thou shalt call me Ishi; and shalt call me no more Baali”. Hebrew (WLC) 2:18: אִישִׁ֑י. Brenton’s Greek 2:18: ὁ ἀνήρ μου. Brenton’s own English (https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/HOS02.htm) prints: “My husband”. KJV Hosea 2:7: “I will go and return to my first husband”. Hebrew (WLC) 2:9: אִישִׁ֣י הָֽרִאשֹׁ֔ון. title: “the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim … came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon” or “the fourth year of Jehoiakim … the first year of Nebuchadrezzar”?
summary: Daniel 1:1 has Nebuchadnezzar, “king of Babylon”, come against Jerusalem “in the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim”. Jeremiah 25:1 says the fourth year of Jehoiakim “was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon”. Jeremiah 46:2 puts his smiting of Pharaohnecho in that fourth year.
text: KJV Daniel 1:1: “In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem”. KJV Jeremiah 25:1: “in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, that was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon”. KJV Jeremiah 46:2: “Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim”.
reasoning: Daniel 1:1 names Nebuchadnezzar “king of Babylon” in the third year of Jehoiakim. Jeremiah 25:1 gives the fourth year of Jehoiakim as the first year of Nebuchadrezzar, and 46:2 gives that fourth year for the battle at Carchemish. Read as worded, the king is called king of Babylon one year before his first year. The two statements could both stand if the two books count the years of a reign by different methods, or if the title in Daniel 1:1 is the title used of him when the event is told; neither passage says how the years are counted.
scope: No tag is proposed: the record compares the wording of the KJV only, and does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek. It does not say that either book is mistaken, and it does not say that the siege of Daniel 1:1 and the battle of Jeremiah 46:2 are the same event. The spellings Nebuchadnezzar and Nebuchadrezzar are the KJV’s two spellings of the name and are not the point.
